card.headline: Did you know there are better words than *"very sleepy"*?

beats.speech: Did you know there are better words than very sleepy? Here are three.
Drowsy: Ana yawns at night. She feels drowsy.
Exhausted: She worked all day. She is exhausted.
Groggy: She wakes up slowly. She feels groggy.
Which word will you use? Comment yours!

language_approval.notes: All 5 beats natural B1; drowsy (yawning at night), exhausted, groggy (just woke up) are fair very-sleepy synonyms in correct senses. One fix: beat 3 example "It is very late." -> "She worked all day." (removed very in a Stop-Saying-very video; exhausted = very tired from effort, lateness alone does not fit). Footage fields untouched; caps OK; no policy issues.
